Motivation

Encoder Decoder models produces garbage output on the intel_xpu backend (page_size > 1). Two root causes in the paged encoder-decoder KV path:

  1. Cross-attention page table not converted to page numbers. encoder_page_table was left token-granular while the paged kernel interprets its entries as page indices — the decoder attended to wrong encoder KV.
  2. Decoder KV region not page-aligned. e.g. whisper reserves max_source_positions (1500) encoder slots, but 1500 % page_size ≠ 0, so the decoder KV started mid-page. The paged decode kernel/allocator assume each sequence begins on a page boundary (physical slot = page * page_size + i % page_size), so decoder tokens were read/written at wrong slots.

Modifications

Reserve a page-aligned number of encoder slots (ceil_align(encoder_len, page_size), e.g. 1500 → 1536) so the decoder KV starts on a page boundary, while keeping the true encoder length (1500) for what the encoder writes and what cross-attention reads. The extra padding slots are allocated but never written/read.

  • whisper.py — pad_input_ids prepends ceil_align(encoder_len, page_size) dummy tokens; num_image_tokens stays the true length.
  • schedule_batch.py — strip/offset the decoder region by the page-aligned reserve; write encoder KV for only the true length.
  • mem_cache/allocation.py (alloc_for_decode) — read last_loc and write decoder KV at the page-aligned encoder_offset column.
  • xpu_backend.py — stride+divide encoder_page_table into page numbers (cross-attn fix); slice the decoder self-attention page_table from the aligned offset.

All changes use ceil_align(x, page_size), which is the identity when page_size == 1. CUDA Whisper (flashinfer, page_size=1) and every other model are byte-identical no-ops. The paged encoder-decoder decode path is only exercised on XPU today.

Code Review

This pull request updates the encoder-decoder KV cache allocation and padding logic to ensure that the decoder KV region starts on a page boundary, which is required by paged decode kernels (particularly on XPU backends). This is done by introducing page-aligned encoder reserves and adjusting offsets across the scheduler, memory allocator, and model-specific input padding. The reviewer identified critical issues in schedule_batch.py where comparing prefix indices against the page-aligned encoder_reserve instead of the true encoder_len will cause assertion failures and incorrect token stripping when the encoder is fully cached.

@sunjiweiswift @mingfeima I have added tests.

@jmunetong I have updated if len(req.prefix_indices) < encoder_reserve: to if len(req.prefix_indices) < encoder_len:. But keeping it to encoder_reserve would still work because out of supported encoder-decoder models on sglang:

def is_encoder_decoder_model(model_architectures: List[str]):
    models = [
        "WhisperForConditionalGeneration",
        "MllamaForConditionalGeneration",
        "MossVLForConditionalGeneration",
    ]
    return any(model in model_architectures for model in models)

I have adapted the pad_input_ids methods of whisper and mllama to use encoder_reserver as padding length.

moss_vl can only run on the flashinfer backend with page_size=1 right now, so anyway it won't get affected by the change because CUDA is using page size 1 and the flashinfer backend for encoder-decoder models. This issue happens when page_size>1 as decode length is expected to start from offset=0. And our change to infer encoder length ceil_align(len, page_size) returns same output as before for cuda i.e. ceil_align(len, 1)=len

from what i understand, this pr tries to solve the issue of kv cache slot/index for encoder model (e.g. whisper). And flashinfer backend has no such issue because it sets page_size to 1.

overall i would say the logic is correct. But we really need to be careful because this fix now changes core part in sgl such as shedule_batch.py and a non-xpu backend flashinfer, which does not make sense from the first look.

my suggestion is that we support page_size == 1 for xpu attention backend. And solve the efficiency issue within xpu attention backend. sure this would introduce in-efficiency at the first place, how flashinfer handle it ?

If XPU encoder-decoder uses page_size=1, the existing shared layout already works and these common-file changes are unnecessary. They are only needed to support XPU with page_size>1; in that case, the aligned encoder reserve should preferably be modeled as shared metadata instead of recalculated independently in each backend.
